question: 目前全世界有多少等价于H100的算力用于AI大模型的部署与训练

target.what: Worldwide installed AI-accelerator compute capacity expressed in H100-equivalent GPUs (i.e., aggregate accelerator throughput normalized to one NVIDIA H100 SXM as the reference unit), counting both training and inference/deployment use, as a stock at the cutoff date
target.publisher: No official publisher; assembled from vendor shipment/installed-base disclosures, cloud capex and fleet disclosures, and third-party market estimates
target.caveats: Ambiguous: 'H100-equivalent' requires a normalization convention (dense FP16/BF16 throughput vs. sparse, memory bandwidth, interconnect). Working interpretation: total deployed accelerator FLOP/s (or effective training/inference throughput) divided by one H100 SXM's comparable throughput, summed acr

candidates.perspective: NVIDIA data-center revenue and unit disclosures as the dominant supply-side anchor
candidates.hypothesis: NVIDIA holds the majority share of AI accelerator compute; cumulative data-center GPU shipments (A100/H100/H200/GB200 etc.) times per-unit H100-equivalent throughput, plus a non-NVIDIA share uplift, approximates the global stock. Higher NVIDIA DC revenue implies proportionally higher installed H100-equivalent base.
candidates.data_to_find: NVIDIA quarterly Data Center revenue and any disclosed unit shipments or installed-base figures through the quarter ending before 2026-10-24; average selling price per accelerator to convert revenue to units; per-architecture throughput multipliers relative to H100 SXM. Substitute: analyst estimates of NVIDIA AI GPU units shipped per year.
search_hints: NVIDIA H100 H200 GB200 units shipped estimate

candidates.perspective: Hyperscaler and neocloud capex and fleet disclosures
candidates.hypothesis: Aggregate AI-datacenter capex across major cloud operators, divided by cost per H100-equivalent node (including networking and facilities), yields an implied installed H100-equivalent count. Higher capex implies more capacity.
candidates.data_to_find: Capex guidance/actuals for Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, xAI, CoreWeave and other neoclouds for 2024-2026; share of capex attributable to AI accelerators vs. facilities/other; cost per H100-equivalent server including networking. Substitute: disclosed GPU counts (e.g., Meta's 600k H100-equivalent, xAI Colossus GPU counts).

candidates.perspective: Datacenter power capacity as a physical constraint on deployed compute
candidates.hypothesis: AI datacenter power capacity (MW) times utilization times H100-equivalent throughput per MW gives an upper-bound estimate of deployed compute. Constrains the stock from the power side.
candidates.data_to_find: Global AI-datacenter IT load in MW (2024-2026), share dedicated to AI accelerators, typical rack power density and H100-equivalent per MW (e.g., H100 at ~10-15 kW per 8-GPU node). Substitute: total datacenter power and AI share.

candidates.perspective: Non-NVIDIA accelerator supply (TPU, Trainium, MI300, Gaudi) as a coverage gap
candidates.hypothesis: Google TPU, AWS Trainium/Inferentia, AMD MI300/MI350 and others add capacity not captured by NVIDIA shipments; converting their throughput to H100-equivalents and adding to the NVIDIA base closes the coverage gap. Larger non-NVIDIA share raises the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Estimated TPU and Trainium deployment volumes (Google/AWS disclosures, analyst estimates), AMD data-center GPU revenue and units, and per-chip throughput ratios vs. H100 SXM. Substitute: share of AI compute that is non-NVIDIA from industry surveys.
search_hints: AMD MI300 MI350 data center GPU revenue

candidates.perspective: Third-party market research and forecasters of AI compute installed base
candidates.hypothesis: Published estimates of global AI accelerator installed base or AI compute (in H100-equivalents or exaFLOP/s) provide a direct cross-check; these aggregate the same supply data and can anchor or validate other routes.
candidates.data_to_find: Reports from Epoch AI, SemiAnalysis, TrendForce, Omdia, IDC, or similar giving global AI accelerator shipments or installed H100-equivalent compute for 2024-2026. Note methodology and whether they count stock or shipments.
search_hints: Epoch AI H100 equivalent global compute
global AI compute H100 equivalents estimate

candidates.perspective: Conversion ratios between accelerator generations and H100
candidates.hypothesis: The H100-equivalent conversion depends on per-chip throughput multipliers (H200 ~1.5x, B200 ~2.5-4x, GB200 NVL72 per-GPU, TPU v5/v6, MI300X). Accurate multipliers are needed to convert unit counts to H100-equivalents; errors here scale the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Dense FP16/BF16 and FP8 throughput specs for H100 SXM, H200, B200, GB200, MI300X, TPU v5p/v6e, Trainium2; a stated normalization convention (dense vs sparse). Substitute: published H100-equivalent conversion tables.
search_hints: H100 vs B200 vs GB200 throughput comparison
H100 equivalent conversion TPU Trainium MI300

candidates.perspective: Prior-year estimates of global AI compute to establish growth trajectory
candidates.hypothesis: If earlier estimates of global H100-equivalent compute exist (e.g., for 2023-2025), applying observed growth rates to the latest anchor yields the 2026 stock. Growth has been steep, so the trajectory constrains the plausible range.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published estimates of global AI accelerator compute in H100-equivalents for 2023, 2024, 2025; year-over-year growth in NVIDIA DC revenue and accelerator shipments as a proxy. Substitute: cumulative shipment estimates by year.

candidates.perspective: Frontier labs and large enterprises disclosing their own cluster sizes
candidates.hypothesis: Summing disclosed cluster sizes of major AI labs (OpenAI/Stargate, Anthropic, xAI, Meta, Google DeepMind, Microsoft, Amazon) plus an allowance for the long tail of enterprises gives a bottom-up floor; disclosed clusters are a large share of total.
candidates.data_to_find: Disclosed GPU counts and types for major labs and Stargate-type projects as of 2026; enterprise/sovereign AI cluster announcements. Convert each to H100-equivalents and sum, then estimate the uncovered long tail share.

They share the same underlying measurement and are not independent.

Epoch AI Data Centers explorer coverage: 74 large DCs with 12.5M H100e (p41) and 86 sites covering 44% of global compute (p57/p80/p81). These are consistent with a global total of ~28M H100e (12.5M / 0.44) and share the same source.

Meta Prometheus capacity: p30 says 536k H100e as of Aug 31, 2026; p44 says 763k H100e (undated, likely later or different scope). Both are Epoch-derived but differ by ~42%, possibly due to timing or definition (IT power vs. chip count).
Google holds ~5M H100e (p73), ~25% of world total (p74), and TPUs alone are ~4M H100e (p75). These are internally consistent (5M / 0.25 = 20M world total) and share the same Epoch AI source.

Epoch AI estimates of AI compute use by major labs (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta) for Dec 2025 sum to ~5.5M H100e, which is a subset of the global stock. They share the same methodology and source.

NVIDIA disclosed cumulative Hopper shipments of 4M GPUs (p143) and Blackwell/Rubin shipments of 6M GPUs (3M Hopper-equivalent, p145/p146). These are vendor disclosures and provide a floor for NVIDIA's installed base.

Bizety estimates: total high-end NVIDIA GPU deployments surpassed 10M through 2025 (p19) and a world with 10M depreciated but capable GPUs (p21). These are the same underlying estimate.
TrendForce: global datacenter power demand 123 GW in 2025 (p94) and AI server share ~25% (p95), implying ~31 GW for AI servers. This is a power-side constraint.

methods.rationale: Direct use of the most recent published estimate of global AI compute stock in H100-equivalents (p39, ~20M as of Aug 2026). methods.rationale: Uses the Epoch AI extrapolation to September 2026 (p56, 31.6M H100e), which is the most recent model-based estimate of the global stock. This is an extrapolation from end-2025 delivered capacity using a 9-month doubling period, so it carries model risk. methods.rationale: Coverage-based scaling: the 74 large data centers tracked by Epoch AI contain 12.5M H100e (p41) and represent 44% of global AI compute (p57). Dividing gives an implied global total of ~28.4M H100e. This route uses the same underlying Epoch AI data but applies a different aggregation (coverage ratio) and thus provides a partially independent check on the level. The main assumption is that the 44% coverage share is accurate and applies to the same set of facilities as the 12.5M figure.

assessment.note: All are Epoch-AI-derived aggregates of global AI compute in H100-equivalents. p55 (20.3M end-2025) and p56 (31.6M Sept-2026) are the same series at two dates; p69/p140/p254 (15M, Jan-2026 page) is an earlier vintage of the same series; p39 (20M, Aug-2026) is a secondary restatement of the same underlying Epoch work. They are not independent measurements — they share one dataset and one normalization convention (peak 8-bit ops).

Epoch explorer coverage: 12.5M H100e across 74 sites at 44% coverage implies ~28M global; the 86-site/44% figures are the same coverage statistic restated. Same source, so this is one route, not several.

Google ~5M H100e = ~25% of world implies ~20M world total (April 2026 vintage). TPU-only ~4M (CI 3.1–4.5M) is consistent with 5M total including GPUs. Same Epoch source; the 25% share is the load-bearing number.
Five US hyperscalers >70% of global compute and China ~5% are consistent with a world total dominated by a handful of owners; both from the same Epoch analysis.

Meta Prometheus is 536k H100e at 471 MW (Aug 2026, Epoch) but 763k H100e in the Aug-2026 secondary report. Different vintages/definitions of the same facility; the 536k figure is the primary Epoch page and is preferred. Either way this is a single-site datum, not a world total.

Hopper 4M cumulative (2023–2025) plus 6M Blackwell/Rubin shipped (3M Hopper-equivalent) gives a shipment-side cross-check on the ~10M high-end NVIDIA units deployed through 2025. p19/p21 (10M high-end NVIDIA GPUs) are consistent with this shipment arithmetic.

Epoch Feb-2025 NVIDIA-only estimate: 4M H100e (median 3.9e21 FLOP/s, CI 3.6–4.7e21) with 2.3x/yr growth (CI 2.2–2.5x). This is the historical anchor for the growth route; it is NVIDIA-only and predates the target by ~20 months.

Per-chip dense FP16 throughputs used for H100-equivalent normalization: H100/H200 989 TFLOPS, B200 2250, A100 312, V100 125. These define the conversion convention and are internally consistent (B200/H100 ≈ 2.28x).

Power-side constraints: 123 GW global DC capacity 2025 with ~25% AI-server share (~31 GW) vs Epoch's ~10 GW chip draw for tracked AI chips. The gap is consistent with AI-server power including networking/cooling/older gear and with Epoch tracking only leading chips; these are bounds, not equal measures.

Non-NVIDIA accelerator volumes: Trainium2/2.5 ~1.9M lifecycle units and Google TPU ~2.4M shipments in 2025. These are unit counts, not H100-equivalents; conversion requires per-chip multipliers (TPUv7 ≈ 2.3x H100 per p127, discarded but indicative).

Dec-2025 lab-level compute use (OpenAI 1.74M, GDM 1.58M, Anthropic 1.19M, Meta 1.0M H100e) sums to ~5.5M for four labs, consistent with a world total in the tens of millions and with hyperscaler dominance.

methods.label: m1

p39.role: Worldwide total AI chip compute capacity in use, H100-equivalent (current stock) as of 2026-08-03

methods.rationale: Direct anchor: a secondary restatement of Epoch AI's worldwide H100e stock as of Aug-2026. Closest single number to the Oct-2026 cutoff; uncertainty is the lognormal spread code applies plus the ~2-month lag.

methods.label: m2

p55.role: Epoch AI estimated global AI compute delivered, cumulative H100-equivalents at end of 2025

a1.role: Growth factor from end-2025 to Oct-2026, derived from the Epoch 20.3M→31.6M trajectory

methods.rationale: Growth route: carry the end-2025 Epoch delivered-capacity figure forward to Oct-2026 using the observed 20.3M→31.6M trajectory. Shares the Epoch dataset with m1, so not independent, but uses a different vintage and an explicit growth assumption.

methods.label: m4

p73.role: Google AI compute capacity in H100-equivalents (stock), estimate

p74.role: Google share of world total AI compute capacity

methods.rationale: Share route: Google's ~5M H100e divided by its ~25% share implies ~20M world total (April-2026 vintage). Independent of the coverage route in construction but shares the Epoch underlying dataset; the main failure mode is that the 25% share is a rough estimate.

methods.label: m5

p95.role: AI server share of global datacenter power demand capacity, 2025

a3.role: H100-equivalent per MW of AI IT power, calibrated from Meta Prometheus and Colossus 1

methods.rationale: Power-side route: 123 GW global DC capacity × 25% AI-server share × ~1100 H100e/MW. This is a capacity bound rather than a realized stock, and the 2025 power figures lag the Oct-2026 cutoff; the conversion factor is calibrated from two observed facilities. Failure modes: AI-server share may have risen toward 33% by 2026, and the H100e/MW factor varies with chip mix.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 4 blocks; median of blocks: this block is the median
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 4 blocks; median of blocks: this block is the median
weight_basis.m3: B3 of 4 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m4: B4 of 4 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

kept.applies_when: Used to convert AI IT power capacity to H100-equivalent compute.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that the average H100e per MW across the global fleet is well outside 800–1500.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
